definitions: To believe someone's statement or accept their innocence, even when there is some uncertainty or lack of complete proof.
To assume someone is telling the truth or acting with good intentions, rather than being suspicious, when the evidence is not conclusive.
examples: I'll give him the benefit of the doubt this time, but if it happens again, there will be consequences.
Despite the conflicting stories, the judge decided to give the defendant the benefit of the doubt.
She seemed a bit hesitant, but I gave her the benefit of the doubt and trusted her explanation.
lemma: give the benefit of the doubt
synonyms: err on the side of leniency
source: give the benefit of the doubt
